title: An update's one-time records repair can wipe a lift's records for good if the app closes mid-way
what: When a member updates from an older version, a one-time repair rebuilds the personal records of every lift that had a long set (more than 12 reps) stored the old way. For each lift it first deletes all its records, then writes them again from the sets. These two steps are not done together. If the app is closed or killed in between, that lift is left with no records, and on the next start the repair no longer finds the lift (its old rows are gone), so it is never rebuilt. The member's records list and Home's strength numbers miss that lift until a workout of it is edited or deleted.
expected: Each lift's delete and rebuild happen as one step, as the newer lighter-set repair already does, so a closed app keeps the old records and simply retries next start.
who: members updating from a version before 13 Oct 2026, or restoring an older backup
how_often: rare: only if the app closes during the repair on first start after the update
fix_line: Wrap each lift's rebuild in one step, the same way the lighter-set repair does

items.reason: Fresh install: repairs find nothing and mark done. Update: three one-time record repairs run at start and again after a restore; one can lose a lift's records (new finding), one can skip its second half (existing). Older native pieces are treated as optional everywhere in the rest card. Watch and phone on different versions: compared by version name (existing finding: update shown before Play has one; minus 15 s silent on an old phone). Sideload vs Play watch signing: existing finding. Saved plate setups and target choices from another version fall back to defaults. Panel cache after deploy does not apply to phone services.

Trial or plan end: the watch lock is handed over, but only at the next set (existing finding). Member leaves the gym: trainer video links are forgotten. Year end: January keeps last year's review beside this year so far. Moving a workout keeps date and time agreeing and never lands in the future. A clock set back does not block the watch pop-up for ever. Owner changes phone: a restore re-runs the record repairs. App not opened for months: an old open workout is resumed without its date (existing finding). Leap day: no day-of-year math here. Staff leaving and gym pause do not apply to these member phone services.

The record fixes are written for existing users (run once per install on update). The watch install card counts any saved workout, so existing members see it too. Save as routine and the rest-alert question key off present state, not install age.
Existing users get each repair at their first start after the update, and again after restoring an older backup.
Rule applied: no new-installs-only flow without a path found in this area.

The only new-since mark here is the watch pop-up's New on your watch lines. A brand-new install with a matching watch sees none; a watch from before version labels gets the last 3 versions' watch lines, which are new to it. A new install whose Play watch build lags is told of an update that is not out yet (existing finding).
Rule applied: no mark on something old to the member beyond the existing lagging-watch finding.
